chapter: Ben Webster and Jim and Andy's
title: Duke Ellington's refusal and Ben's walkout
summary: Webster asks Duke to let Maxwell sit in; Duke refuses and Ben leaves, handing Duke the check.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: But he would go on these long harrangues about that. Now, one night he went over to Duke Ellington and said, Benny Goodman's first trumpet player is here, Jim Maxwell, and

he said he knows every arrangement you've ever made. He said, he loves the band, it's the only band he likes. Could he sit in? And Duke got very salty and made some remark, I don't said, "I don't want any ofay in the band." want one of these guys sitting in my band. Actually, he / And really hurt my feelings. But Ben got furious. He just walked out. He said, "come on," took me by the arm, grabbed my wife, and I said, "hey, wait, I've got to pay the check." He told the waiters, "give the check to him -- Duke Ellington."

And he walked out, he didn't go back for three days. Just out of solidarity of friendship. I kept telling him, don't be silly, you know, I understand how he feels in the first place, and he's got a stinky day because it's ridiculous for him to say he didn't want white guys in the band, because I don't know whether Barney Bigard is white or not, or Juan Tizol.

I don't know. He looked white. I don't know if black is a state of mind or the color of your skin. But it was kind of a funny remark. You know, years later, obviously he didn't give a damn one way or the other.
